worksheets.title: Simplifying Ratios and Dividing in a Ratio

fluency_questions.prompt: Simplify each whole-number ratio to its simplest form:
Simplify each ratio involving decimals, fractions, or mixed units:
Divide each quantity in the given ratio:
Find the unknown value $x$ in each equivalent ratio or scale:

parts.label: c
parts.question: Scale $1 : 500$; drawing length $6\text{ cm}$, real length $x\text{ m}$

parts.label: d
parts.question: Scale $1 : 200\,000$; map distance $4.5\text{ cm}$, real distance $x\text{ km}$

application_questions.question: A concrete footing mix uses cement, sand, and gravel in the ratio $1 : 2 : 4$ by mass. If $420\text{ kg}$ of dry concrete mix is prepared, find the mass of (a) cement, (b) sand, and (c) gravel required.
Two business partners, Noah and Zara, invest in a Melbourne coffee roastery in the ratio $5 : 7$. If Noah invested $\$45\,000$, how much did Zara invest, and what was their combined investment?

On a Vicmap topographic map with a scale of $1 : 50\,000$, the straight-line distance between two huts in the Alpine National Park is $7.6\text{ cm}$. Calculate the actual ground distance in kilometres.
The three interior angles of a triangle are in the ratio $2 : 3 : 4$. Find the size of each angle and classify the triangle by its angles.

reasoning_questions.question: In a fruit punch, the ratio of orange juice to pineapple juice is $3 : 2$, and the ratio of pineapple juice to sparkling water is $4 : 5$. Combine these into a single three-part ratio $\text{orange} : \text{pineapple} : \text{water}$ in simplest form.

Currently, the ratio of red marbles to blue marbles in a jar is $3 : 5$, and there are $64$ marbles in total. How many red marbles must be ADDED to the jar so that the new ratio of red to blue becomes $1 : 1$?

fluency_questions.prompt: Convert each speed or rate to the specified unit:
Calculate the unit price per $100\text{ g}$ or per $1\text{ L}$ for each grocery item:

parts.label: c
parts.question: $1.5\text{ L}$ of olive oil for $\$18.90$ ($\text{per } 1\text{ L}$)

application_questions.question: A supermarket sells Australian almonds in three pack sizes: Pack A ($200\text{ g}$ for $\$5.20$), Pack B ($500\text{ g}$ for $\$11.50$), and Pack C ($800\text{ g}$ for $\$19.20$). Calculate the cost per $100\text{ g}$ for each pack and determine the best buy.
application_questions.answer: Pack A $= \$2.60/100\text{ g}$, Pack B $= \$2.30/100\text{ g}$, Pack C $= \$2.40/100\text{ g}$; Pack B is the best buy.

application_questions.question: A family car consumes $6.8\text{ L}$ of petrol per $100\text{ km}$ on the Hume Freeway. (a) How many litres of petrol are needed for a $450\text{ km}$ drive? (b) At $\$1.95\text{ per litre}$, what is the fuel cost for the trip?
A V/Line train travels $75\text{ km}$ from Melbourne to Geelong in $50\text{ minutes}$ ($ rac{5}{6}\text{ hour}$). Calculate the train's average speed in $\text{km/h}$ and in $\text{m/s}$.

Tap A fills a $600\text{ L}$ trough at $12\text{ L/min}$, and Tap B fills the same trough at $8\text{ L/min}$. If both taps are turned on together, how many minutes does it take to fill the $600\text{ L}$ trough?

reasoning_questions.question: A cyclist rides $30\text{ km}$ uphill at $15\text{ km/h}$ ($2\text{ hours}$) and returns $30\text{ km}$ downhill along the same road at $30\text{ km/h}$ ($1\text{ hour}$). Show that her overall average speed for the $60\text{ km}$ round trip is $20\text{ km/h}$, NOT $\dfrac{15 + 30}{2} = 22.5\text{ km/h}$.
reasoning_questions.answer: Total distance $= 60\text{ km}$ and total time $= 2 + 1 = 3\text{ hours}$, so $\text{Average speed} = \dfrac{60}{3} = 20\text{ km/h}$.

reasoning_questions.question: Explain why converting $1\text{ m/s}$ to $\text{km/h}$ multiplies by $3.6$: show where the $3600$ and $1000$ come from in the unit conversion.
reasoning_questions.answer: In $1\text{ hour}$ ($3600\text{ s}$), an object moving at $1\text{ m/s}$ travels $3600\text{ m} = \dfrac{3600}{1000}\text{ km} = 3.6\text{ km}$, so $1\text{ m/s} = 3.6\text{ km/h}$.
